claim: E3M1 closes each street with a mass standing 3.86 to 5.80 bodies above the road (floor tile 379, sky ceiling), outside the map's edge, blocking (cstat 1), with a parallax sector of no height behind it so the sky comes down over it. Seen from the road the face is the road sector's own wall record: tile 414 (plaster over brick) at shade 24, not lit apart from the masonry; the masses' own records (400, 401, 108 at shade -8) face the road but the engine draws a step from the viewer's side, so they are not seen. In Gravesend an unlit end read as a dark block at 30,000 units, and a mouth split between two districts was built as two masses.
evidence: E3M1 s0 (floor -90112, sky -188416) and s339 (floor -57344), backed by s338 and s340 (floor = ceiling = 8192, ceiling_stat 3); E3M1 s343 (floor -90112, tile 379), backed by s342; road-side walls 47, 49, 1535, 22, 26, 28, 222, 816, 947: tile 414, shade 24, cstat 1
NBlood/source/build/src/engine.cpp:4801-4833 (classicDrawBunches): the lower step is drawn from the viewer sector's own wall, from nextwall only when cstat&2
use: bloodmap.street.end_wall gives the mass; make it blocking and declare its zero-exit to the geometry audit; a sky backing of no height is exempt from the lowered-sky rule. A face you want lit must be lit on the road sector's own wall records, which are what the street sees. Other ways to end a city are a waterfront (DWE3M10) or a chasm (DWE3M1).
